data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol is an epistemic tombstone with monotonic evidence generations that forbids reclamation from ever writing into a generation that has produced evidence; it must durably record a generation registry and cryptographic commitments to each generation's output.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Generation counter overflow or exhaustion.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Storage exhaustion because completed generations cannot be reclaimed even when their evidence is long obsolete.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Registry corruption causes generation aliasing, permitting write-after-reclaim displacement.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Evidence is tagged with a monotonic generation counter (problem-id, gen, causal-hash). Reclamation may allocate new generations but may never reclaim storage occupied by a generation that produced at least one evidence artifact. The protocol durably records a generation registry mapping problem-ids to current generations and completed-evidence counts per generation. This transforms silent displacement from an overwrite risk into an explicit allocation failure, because the address space of completed generations is permanently reserved.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
